nodes.name: Sol
nodes.description: The heart of our Solar System, Sol is a G-type main-sequence star (a yellow dwarf). It accounts for 99.8% of the system's total mass. Its energy, produced by nuclear fusion in its core, radiates outward, making life on Earth possible.

nodes.name: Mercury
nodes.description: The smallest planet and closest to the Sun. Mercury is a world of extremes, with scorching daytime temperatures (430°C) and frigid nights (-180°C). It has no real atmosphere, only a thin exosphere, and its cratered surface resembles Earth's Moon.

nodes.name: Venus
nodes.description: Earth's 'sister planet' in size, but a hellish world. Venus suffers from a runaway greenhouse effect, trapping heat under a thick, toxic atmosphere of CO2 and sulfuric acid clouds. Its surface pressure is 92 times that of Earth, and it's the hottest planet in the system.

nodes.name: Wander (Dead)
nodes.description: The third planet from the Sun and the only known astronomical object to harbor life. It is an ocean world, with 71% of its surface covered in liquid water, protected by a strong magnetic field and a breathable nitrogen-oxygen atmosphere.

nodes.name: Luna
nodes.description: Earth's only natural satellite and the largest relative to its host planet in the Solar System. It is tidally locked, always showing the same face to Earth. Its cratered, airless surface is composed of dark volcanic 'maria' and bright, ancient highlands.

nodes.name: Mars
nodes.description: The fourth planet, known as the 'Red Planet' due to iron oxide (rust) on its surface. It's a cold desert world with a very thin CO2 atmosphere, polar ice caps, and the largest volcano (Olympus Mons) and canyon (Valles Marineris) in the Solar System.

nodes.name: Phobos
nodes.description: The larger and innermost of Mars's two moons. It is a small, lumpy, and heavily cratered body, thought to be a captured asteroid. Phobos orbits so close to Mars that it will either crash into the planet or be torn apart into a ring in about 50 million years.

nodes.name: Deimos
nodes.description: The smaller and outer of Mars's two moons. Like its sibling Phobos, Deimos is a small, dark, and irregularly shaped body, likely a captured C-type asteroid. Its surface is smoother than Phobos's, as many of its craters are filled with fine dust (regolith).

nodes.name: The Main Belt
nodes.description: A torus-shaped region of space between Mars and Jupiter, occupied by millions of asteroids. This is leftover material from the early Solar System that was prevented from forming a planet by Jupiter's immense gravity. The largest object in the belt is the dwarf planet Ceres.

nodes.name: Jupiter
nodes.description: The fifth planet and the largest in the Solar System. This gas giant is more than twice as massive as all other planets combined. It's known for its colorful cloud bands of ammonia ice and the Great Red Spot, a giant storm that has raged for centuries.
nodes.resonanceNote: 5:2 mean-motion resonance with Saturn — pumps eccentricity.
nodes.orbitalStabilityDetails: Metastable; generally long-lived (>100 Myr to Gyr), but dynamically packed and perturbation-sensitive. Drivers: Marginal Hill spacing (Delta=7.95).

nodes.name: Jupiter's Rings
nodes.description: A faint ring system composed of three main parts: an inner 'halo', a bright 'main' ring, and an outer 'gossamer' ring. Unlike Saturn's icy rings, Jupiter's are made of small, dark dust particles, likely kicked up from its small inner moons by meteoroid impacts.

nodes.name: Io
nodes.description: The innermost Galilean moon, Io is the most volcanically active body in the Solar System. It is caught in a tidal 'tug-of-war' between Jupiter and the other moons, which flexes its interior and powers hundreds of volcanoes that erupt sulfur and lava.
nodes.resonanceNote: Laplace resonance chain (1:2:4) with Io/Europa/Ganymede — locked and tidally heated.

nodes.name: Europa
nodes.description: A smooth, ice-covered world with a young surface crisscrossed by cracks and streaks. It is a prime candidate for life, as evidence strongly suggests a deep, liquid saltwater ocean exists beneath its 15-25 km thick ice shell, kept warm by tidal heating.
nodes.resonanceNote: Laplace resonance chain (1:2:4) with Io/Europa/Ganymede — locked and tidally heated.

nodes.name: Ganymede
nodes.description: The largest moon in the Solar System, even larger than the planet Mercury. Ganymede is a differentiated icy world and is the only moon known to have its own magnetic field. Its surface has both dark, ancient, cratered regions and lighter, younger, grooved terrain.
nodes.resonanceNote: Laplace resonance chain (1:2:4) with Io/Europa/Ganymede — locked and tidally heated.

nodes.name: Callisto
nodes.description: The outermost Galilean moon, Callisto has the oldest and most heavily cratered surface in the Solar System, indicating a lack of geological activity. It is a geologically 'dead' world, composed of roughly equal parts rock and ice. It may also hide a subsurface ocean.

nodes.name: Saturn
nodes.description: The sixth planet and the second-largest, Saturn is a gas giant famous for its spectacular ring system. It is the least dense planet—it would float in water. Its atmosphere is a pale yellow, striped with bands of ammonia ice clouds and powerful winds.
nodes.resonanceNote: 5:2 mean-motion resonance with Jupiter — pumps eccentricity.
nodes.orbitalStabilityDetails: Metastable; generally long-lived (>100 Myr to Gyr), but dynamically packed and perturbation-sensitive. Drivers: Marginal Hill spacing (Delta=7.95).

nodes.name: Saturn's Rings
nodes.description: The most extensive and complex ring system in the Solar System. The rings are not solid but are made of billions of particles of water ice, with some rock and dust, ranging in size from a grain of sand to a house. They are incredibly thin, perhaps only 10 meters thick.

nodes.name: Titan
nodes.description: Saturn's largest moon and the only moon with a thick, Earth-like atmosphere (though it's 95% nitrogen and toxic). Its surface is -179°C, cold enough for liquid methane and ethane to form rivers, lakes, and seas in a 'hydrological' cycle similar to Earth's water cycle.

nodes.name: Enceladus
nodes.description: A small, bright white icy moon that is one of the most compelling places to search for life. It ejects massive plumes of water, ice, and organic molecules from 'tiger stripes' near its south pole, revealing a global subsurface ocean of liquid saltwater.
nodes.resonanceNote: 2:1 mean-motion resonance with Dione — pumps eccentricity.

nodes.name: Mimas
nodes.description: The smallest and innermost of Saturn's major moons, Mimas is nicknamed the 'Death Star' moon. It is dominated by the Herschel crater, a massive impact basin 139 km wide—nearly a third of the moon's own diameter—that almost shattered the icy body.
nodes.resonanceNote: 2:1 mean-motion resonance with Tethys — pumps eccentricity.

nodes.name: Rhea
nodes.description: Saturn's second-largest moon, Rhea is a heavily cratered, airless body of ice and rock. Its surface is ancient, with one hemisphere being brighter and more cratered than the other. Its surface also features bright, 'wispy' streaks, which are exposed ice cliffs.

nodes.name: Iapetus
nodes.description: Saturn's 'yin-yang' moon, Iapetus is famous for its dramatic two-tone coloration. Its leading hemisphere is as dark as coal, while its trailing hemisphere is as bright as fresh snow. It also possesses a massive, 20-km-high equatorial ridge.

nodes.name: Uranus
nodes.description: The seventh planet, an ice giant tipped on its side. Uranus rotates at a 98-degree angle, likely from a past collision, causing extreme seasons where its poles face the Sun for 42 years at a time. Its blue-green color comes from methane in its H-He atmosphere.

nodes.name: Uranus' Rings
nodes.description: Uranus is surrounded by 13 known rings. Unlike Saturn's bright, icy rings, these are extremely dark and narrow, composed of particles as dark as coal, likely water ice mixed with radiation-processed organic compounds. They were the first to be discovered after Saturn's.

nodes.name: Titania
nodes.description: The largest of Uranus's moons. This icy, rocky world shows signs of past geological activity. Its surface is cut by a system of enormous canyons and fault valleys, some stretching for 1,000 miles, indicating its interior expanded and cracked the crust long ago.

nodes.name: Oberon
nodes.description: The outermost and second-largest of the major Uranian moons. Oberon has the most ancient and heavily cratered surface of Uranus's moons, showing little sign of past geological activity. Its dark, reddish surface is covered in impact craters, some with bright rays of ice.

nodes.name: Ariel
nodes.description: The brightest and youngest-surfaced of Uranus's moons. Ariel shows clear signs of geologic activity, with vast, interconnected canyons and fault valleys. Smooth plains suggest that 'cryovolcanism' (ice volcanoes) may have once resurfaced parts of the moon.

nodes.name: Neptune
nodes.description: The eighth and most distant planet, Neptune is a dark, cold ice giant whipped by supersonic winds. It has a vivid blue color from methane in its atmosphere. It was the first planet found through mathematical prediction rather than direct observation.
nodes.resonanceNote: 3:2 mean-motion resonance with Pluto-Charon Barycenter — protects against close approaches.

nodes.name: Neptune's Rings
nodes.description: Neptune is encircled by five faint, dark rings. They are notable for containing unstable, bright clumps of dust called 'arcs,' which are thought to be held in place by the gravity of the small moon Galatea. These rings are dusty and relatively young.

nodes.name: Triton
nodes.description: Neptune's largest moon and likely a captured Kuiper Belt Object. It is one of the coldest worlds known (-235°C), yet it is geologically active, with geysers of nitrogen gas erupting from its icy surface. It orbits Neptune 'backwards' in a retrograde orbit.

nodes.name: Kuiper Belt
nodes.description: A vast, doughnut-shaped ring of icy bodies beyond the orbit of Neptune, from about 30 to 50 AU. It is a reservoir of comets and contains many dwarf planets, including Pluto. This is a cold, distant region containing remnants from the formation of the Solar System.

nodes.name: Pluto
nodes.description: A dwarf planet in the Kuiper Belt, formerly classified as the ninth planet. It is a complex world of ice mountains and frozen nitrogen plains. Its highly eccentric orbit sometimes brings it closer to the Sun than Neptune. It has five known moons.
nodes.resonanceNote: 3:2 mean-motion resonance with Neptune — protects against close approaches.
nodes.orbitalStabilityDetails: Metastable; generally long-lived (>100 Myr to Gyr), but dynamically packed and perturbation-sensitive. Drivers: its orbit crosses Neptune's — which on its own would be unstable — but a locked mean-motion resonance keeps their conjunctions away from the crossing point, so it stays stable.

nodes.name: Charon
nodes.description: Pluto's largest moon, so large (half of Pluto's diameter) that the two are considered a binary dwarf planet system. They orbit a common barycenter located in the space between them. Charon is tidally locked to Pluto, so they both always show the same face to each other.
nodes.resonanceNote: 3:2 mean-motion resonance with Neptune — protects against close approaches.
nodes.orbitalStabilityDetails: Metastable; generally long-lived (>100 Myr to Gyr), but dynamically packed and perturbation-sensitive. Drivers: its orbit crosses Neptune's — which on its own would be unstable — but a locked mean-motion resonance keeps their conjunctions away from the crossing point, so it stays stable.

nodes.name: Ceres Station
nodes.description: The capital of the Belt. A dwarf planet hollowed out and spun up to provide 0.3G gravity at the outer tunnels.
nodes.gmNotes: Home to 6 million Belters. The Docks, Medina District, Star Helix Police HQ. 'Down' is toward the surface.

nodes.name: Eros Station
nodes.description: An elongated asteroid spun for gravity. A hub for gambling, vice, and illicit trade.
nodes.gmNotes: The 'Vegas' of the Belt. Site of the Protomolecule incident.

nodes.name: Tycho Station
nodes.description: The largest mobile construction platform in the system. Features a massive central sphere and two counter-rotating habitat rings.
nodes.gmNotes: OPA HQ (Fred Johnson). Currently building the Nauvoo. Can move its orbit.

nodes.name: Anderson Station
nodes.description: A lonely cylinder in the outer belt. A key resupply depot for miners.
nodes.gmNotes: Site of a massacre. Poor ventilation. Gritty industrial aesthetic.

nodes.name: Thoth Station
nodes.description: A stealth-composite station hidden in deep space. Hard to detect on sensors.
nodes.gmNotes: Protogen secret lab. Heavily guarded. The source of the stealth ships.

nodes.name: Ganymede Ag Domes
nodes.description: Massive illuminated domes on the surface of Jupiter's largest moon. Mirrors focus sunlight to grow food.
nodes.gmNotes: The breadbasket of the Belt. Critical strategic resource.

nodes.name: Phoebe: Research Station
nodes.description: A Protogen facility built into the retrograde moon Phoebe.
nodes.gmNotes: Source of the Protomolecule. Dangerous. Burned by Mars.

nodes.name: Lovell City
nodes.description: A massive subterranean city beneath the regolith. The seat of UN power off-Earth.
nodes.gmNotes: Safe, bureaucratic, expensive. 0.16G natural gravity.

nodes.name: Rocinante (Tachi)
nodes.description: Legitimate salvage. A Martian Corvette class. Fast, deadly, and versatile.
nodes.gmNotes: Hero ship. Capable of atmospheric landing and 10G+ burns.

nodes.name: LDSS Nauvoo
nodes.description: The largest ship ever built. Intended for a century-long voyage. A self-contained world.
nodes.gmNotes: Currently docked at Tycho. Future Medina Station.

nodes.name: MCRN Donnager
nodes.description: The Martian flagship. A city in space. Carries two corvettes internally.
nodes.gmNotes: Patrolling Jupiter. Massive railguns. Increased engines for combat Gs.

nodes.name: The Canterbury
nodes.description: A retrofitted colony ship hauling ice from Saturn to Ceres. Old and creaky.
nodes.gmNotes: Remember the Cant. Low thrust, massive mass.

nodes.name: The Razorback
nodes.description: A modified pinnace. A fusion torch with seats. Incredible acceleration.
nodes.gmNotes: Julie Mao's racer. Hard to catch.

nodes.name: MCRN Scirocco
nodes.description: A heavy Martian patrol destroyer. Capable of deploying corvettes.
nodes.gmNotes: Command ship. Heavy armor.

nodes.name: The Pella
nodes.description: A heavy frigate with cruiser-level armament. Fast, aggressive, and packed with torpedoes.
nodes.gmNotes: Free Navy Flagship. Marco Inaros. Hits way above its weight class.

nodes.name: Tethys
nodes.description: A mid-sized moon of almost pure water ice — one of the most reflective bodies in the solar system. Scarred by the enormous Odysseus crater and the vast Ithaca Chasma canyon. It holds Mimas in a 2:1 orbital resonance.
nodes.resonanceNote: 2:1 mean-motion resonance with Mimas — pumps eccentricity.

nodes.name: Dione
nodes.description: An ice moon streaked with bright wispy chasms over a possible deep internal ocean. Its 2:1 orbital resonance with Enceladus is the engine that keeps pumping that smaller moon's eccentricity — and so its famous geysers.
nodes.resonanceNote: 2:1 mean-motion resonance with Enceladus — pumps eccentricity.

nodes.name: Zeta Hydrae II II
nodes.resonanceNote: 3:2 mean-motion resonance with Zeta Hydrae II III — protects against close approaches.
nodes.orbitalStabilityDetails: Likely <1 kyr before major orbital disruption (collision/ejection/infall risk). Drivers: Orbit loosely bound to host (vulnerable to external perturbation).; Critical Hill spacing (Delta=1.75).

nodes.name: Zeta Hydrae II III
nodes.resonanceNote: 3:2 mean-motion resonance with Zeta Hydrae II II — protects against close approaches.
nodes.orbitalStabilityDetails: Likely <1 kyr before major orbital disruption (collision/ejection/infall risk). Drivers: Orbit loosely bound to host (vulnerable to external perturbation).; Critical Hill spacing (Delta=1.75).

nodes.name: Zeta Hyrdae Station Albete
nodes.description: A small, rotating habitation module designed for long-term scientific observation of a planetary body. Includes sensor arrays and a small centrifuge for gravity.
nodes.gmNotes: Ideal for monitoring a primitive species or studying a gas giant. Vulnerable and lightly armed.

nodes.name: Alpha Leonis B
nodes.orbitalStabilityDetails: Likely <1 kyr before major orbital disruption (collision/ejection/infall risk). Drivers: Binary perturbation-sensitive (sep/Hill=0.36); External critical Hill spacing with Alpha Leonis A (Delta=0.08).

nodes.name: Alpha Leonis C
nodes.orbitalStabilityDetails: Likely <1 kyr before major orbital disruption (collision/ejection/infall risk). Drivers: Binary perturbation-sensitive (sep/Hill=0.36); External critical Hill spacing with Alpha Leonis A (Delta=0.08).

nodes.name: Alpha Leonis b
nodes.orbitalStabilityDetails: Likely <1 kyr before major orbital disruption (collision/ejection/infall risk). Drivers: Orbit exceeds host's stable Hill sphere (stolen by external tide).; Tight Hill spacing (Delta=4.79). Predicted outcome: flung out — gravitationally scattered onto an escape trajectory.

nodes.name: Alpha Leonis Barycentre 2 IV
nodes.orbitalStabilityDetails: Likely <1 kyr before major orbital disruption (collision/ejection/infall risk). Drivers: Orbit exceeds host's stable Hill sphere (stolen by external tide).; Tight Hill spacing (Delta=4.79). Predicted outcome: flung out — gravitationally scattered onto an escape trajectory.

nodes.name: TheosisHardened Solar Array
nodes.description: Massive photovoltaic fields designed to harvest the intense output of a close-orbit star.
nodes.gmNotes: High output, but vulnerable. Maintenance crews wear heavy rad-suits.

nodes.name: TheosisWay Station
nodes.description: A dedicated refueling and repair depot located on the Xboat network. Essentially a massive gas station in space.
nodes.gmNotes: Fast turnover. 'W' code. Primary function is maintenance of the express boat network.

system.name: Ossuun System

nodes.name: Ossuun Primary
nodes.description: A quiet orange K-type main-sequence star. Its long-lived, comparatively steady output allowed complex life to develop on Ossuun over billions of years.

nodes.name: Vekk

areas.name: Thermal Lease 01
areas.description: A dispersed field of shielded automated mines and short-duration service shelters operated under an Erbium mineral lease.
areas.gmNotes: The facility is mostly unmanned. Fonqugon contractors remotely model heat expansion and equipment failure from Ossuun orbit.

nodes.description: A tidally locked, metal-rich inner world. Its exposed dayside is mined by automated equipment while service crews operate only during carefully timed maintenance windows.

nodes.name: Talu

areas.name: Kett Shield Refinery
areas.description: A sealed refinery complex processing metals from Talu and the inner system before shipment to Ossuun.
areas.gmNotes: Erbium promotes Talu as proof that heavy industry can remain off Ossuun. Fonqugon confluences dispute how much refinery waste is entering the system's transport economy.

nodes.description: A hot, dry terrestrial world used as the system's principal heavy-industry buffer. Most permanent habitation is sealed and clustered around extraction and refining sites.

nodes.name: Ossuun

areas.name: Siltglass Cradle Basin
areas.description: A broad freshwater shelf containing several ancient cradle colonies and layered communal archives preserved in mineral-rich membranes.

areas.name: Hollow Reed Confluence
areas.description: A modular wetland city whose floating districts host one of Ossuun's largest recurring planetary confluences.

areas.name: Biological Continuity Site 44-C
areas.description: An Erbium-operated nursery and research facility licensed to maintain offworld-compatible cradle-colony cultures.
areas.gmNotes: Site 44-C is a major source of filtration patents, developmental debt, and restricted ambering research.

nodes.description: The Fonqugon homeworld is a warm planet of shallow oceans, freshwater basins, mineral marshes, low continents, and vast floodplains. Two resonant moons create powerful but predictable tides whose interactions with rainfall, groundwater, and biological blooms shaped Fonqugon systems thinking.
nodes.gmNotes: Ossuun's public environmental data is politically contested. Erbium controls much of the orbital sensor infrastructure but does not possess uncontested authority over the planet's confluences or cradle colonies.
nodes.resonanceNote: 5:2 mean-motion resonance with Pebb — pumps eccentricity.

nodes.name: Nebb
nodes.description: The larger and inner of Ossuun's two moons. Its regular motion anchors many tidal forecasts, civic calendars, and historical environmental models.
nodes.resonanceNote: 2:1 mean-motion resonance with Yaru — pumps eccentricity.
nodes.orbitalStabilityDetails: Likely <1 kyr before major orbital disruption (collision/ejection/infall risk). Drivers: Critical Hill spacing (Delta=2.81). Predicted outcome: flung out — gravitationally scattered onto an escape trajectory.

nodes.name: Yaru
nodes.description: An ice-rich outer moon locked in an approximately 2:1 orbital resonance with Nebb. The pair's overlapping tidal cycles are central to Ossuun's ecological forecasting traditions.
nodes.resonanceNote: 2:1 mean-motion resonance with Nebb — pumps eccentricity.
nodes.orbitalStabilityDetails: Likely <1 kyr before major orbital disruption (collision/ejection/infall risk). Drivers: Orbit loosely bound to host (vulnerable to external perturbation).; Critical Hill spacing (Delta=2.81). Predicted outcome: flung out — gravitationally scattered onto an escape trajectory.

nodes.name: Ossuun Integrated Forecast Array
nodes.description: A large orbital observatory integrating weather, tidal, groundwater, biosphere, and relay data for planetary forecasting.
nodes.gmNotes: Erbium routes the array's highest-resolution data through proprietary servers before public release. Several Fonqugon confluences maintain independent instruments to audit its models.
nodes.cargoDescription: Sensor components, water-treatment cultures, replacement relay hardware

nodes.name: Pebb

areas.name: Deep Bloom Survey Vault
areas.description: A buried survey station monitoring Pebb's ice shell, volatile inventory, and possible transient subsurface liquid layers.

nodes.description: A cold super-Earth beyond the primary temperate zone. Most of its water is frozen, making it a major source of volatiles and a long-term target for subsurface research.
nodes.resonanceNote: 5:2 mean-motion resonance with Ossuun — pumps eccentricity.

nodes.name: Ossuun Main Belt
nodes.description: A broad belt of rocky and carbonaceous bodies. Erbium holds many of the largest extraction claims, while Ossuun-based cooperatives operate smaller surveyed clusters.

nodes.name: Dorrun
nodes.description: A ringed gas giant that dominates the outer system. Its atmosphere, moons, and stable gravitational environment support fuel harvesting, research, and long-duration waystations.

nodes.name: Dorrun Rings
nodes.description: A bright ring system composed primarily of water ice mixed with darker rocky material.

nodes.name: Dorrun I
nodes.description: A dense inner moon kept geologically active by Dorrun's tides and its resonance with the outer moon.
nodes.resonanceNote: 2:1 mean-motion resonance with Dorrun II — pumps eccentricity.

nodes.name: Dorrun II
nodes.description: An ice-covered moon in an approximately 2:1 resonance with Dorrun I. Tidal heating may preserve deep liquid layers beneath its surface.
nodes.resonanceNote: 2:1 mean-motion resonance with Dorrun I — pumps eccentricity.

system.notes: Proof-of-concept standalone system for the Fonqugon homeworld. Names beyond Ossuun are provisional.
system.gmNotes: Designed as a stable K-dwarf system with a warm wet homeworld, two resonant moons, Erbium forecasting infrastructure, an inner extraction world, and a distant gas giant.

system.name: Agrio Dysis System

nodes.name: Agrio Dysis Primary
nodes.description: A mature yellow-orange G-type main-sequence star. Its comparatively steady output supports the partially terraformed settlement world Agrio Dysis IV while leaving the inner system hot and dry.

nodes.name: Agrio Dysis I

areas.name: Cauter Leases
areas.description: Shielded automated mines extract dense metals from the permanent dayside. Human maintenance crews enter only during tightly scheduled shutdown windows.
areas.gmNotes: Erbium uses Agrio Dysis I as collateral when negotiating infrastructure loans with the settled government on Agrio Dysis IV.

nodes.description: A small, tidally locked metal-rich world scorched by the primary. Nearly all activity is automated.

nodes.name: Agrio Dysis II

areas.name: Brass Weather Platforms
areas.description: High-altitude robotic platforms collect sulfur compounds and atmospheric feedstock for sealed industrial use elsewhere in the system.

nodes.description: A hot greenhouse world beneath dense carbon dioxide and sulfurous clouds. It supports only remote industrial platforms and short-duration service missions.

nodes.name: Agrio Dysis III

areas.name: Dryline Yard
areas.description: A sealed freight and solar-power complex that stages equipment bound for Agrio Dysis IV and the main belt.
areas.gmNotes: The yard's published emergency reserve is routinely pledged against unrelated corporate debts.

nodes.description: A hot, thin-aired desert world used for solar collection, mineral extraction, and freight staging.

nodes.name: Agrio Dysis IV

areas.name: The Low Plane
areas.description: An immense sunken continental basin bordered by broken mountains and dry uplands. Intense heat, long dry seasons, violent storm fronts, and sudden river flooding define most settled life.

areas.name: Crosswind Junction
areas.description: A major cattle town built around a rail spur, deep well, livestock yard, and seasonal river crossing. Most residents work in freight, repair, water administration, or animal care.

areas.name: Longwater Cooperative
areas.description: A locally maintained network of wells, levees, floodgates, and emergency cisterns serving several settlements outside dependable government support.
areas.gmNotes: The cooperative has evidence that upstream corporate pumping worsens both the dry season and the basin's sudden floods.

areas.name: Erbium Charter House Six
areas.description: A fortified administrative office controlling settlement titles, equipment liens, transport certification, and most recognized water-right records in the central basin.
areas.gmNotes: After major floods, Charter House Six redraws parcel boundaries from corporate survey data. The settled government recognizes the revised registry even when communities have occupied the land for generations.

nodes.description: The primary inhabited world of the Agrio Dysis system. Its largest settled region, the Low Plane, is a vast hot basin of cattle towns, engineered grazing land, river corridors, rail depots, and scattered refuge communities. The planet is breathable and broadly habitable, but terraforming remains uneven and reliable water is controlled through overlapping local, governmental, and corporate claims.
nodes.gmNotes: Agrio Dysis IV is advertised as a frontier opportunity world. Many residents arrived through relocation programs and inherited transport, equipment, land, or water debt. Erbium rarely governs openly; aligned public authorities enforce the registries and contracts that keep settlements dependent.

nodes.name: Rimlight

areas.name: Storm-Eye Observatory
areas.description: A small observatory used to track basin storm fronts, flood seasons, and long-range atmospheric circulation.
areas.gmNotes: Its public forecasts are delayed whenever they conflict with corporate water-allocation models.

nodes.description: Agrio Dysis IV's single moon. Its regular cycle anchors local calendars, flood predictions, and night travel across the Low Plane.

nodes.name: Low Plane Transfer Spindle
nodes.description: A rotating orbital transfer station handling passengers, livestock, freight, and surface-bound settlement equipment.
nodes.gmNotes: Departing residents pass through debt, warrant, and equipment-lien screening before receiving onward transport authorization. The station is publicly administered but its registry systems are supplied and audited by Erbium.
nodes.cargoDescription: Agricultural equipment, livestock feed, pump components, sealed medicine, and outbound hides

nodes.name: Agrio Dysis Main Belt
nodes.description: A broad rocky and carbonaceous belt. Corporate claims dominate the largest bodies, while independent prospectors and settlement cooperatives work smaller surveyed clusters.

nodes.name: Agrio Dysis V
nodes.description: A ringed gas giant supporting fuel harvesting, outer-system traffic, and long-duration survey work.

nodes.name: Agrio Dysis V Rings
nodes.description: A pale ring system composed mostly of water ice mixed with darker carbonaceous material.

nodes.name: Longwatch

areas.name: Cold Pump Depot
areas.description: A buried extraction depot producing water, oxygen, and propellant feedstock for outer-system traffic.

nodes.description: An ice-covered moon whose water reserves make it the outer system's principal refueling site.

nodes.name: Agrio Dysis VI
nodes.description: A distant ice giant marking the practical edge of routine system traffic. Most activity is automated survey work.

system.notes: Standalone system for Agrio Dysis IV, the human refuge and settlement world commonly called the Low Plane.
system.gmNotes: The system is publicly governed, but Erbium-supplied registries, transportation infrastructure, equipment loans, and water-right systems allow the corporation to shape policy without formally administering the world.

system.name: Velis System

nodes.name: Velis Primary
nodes.description: A mature orange K-type main-sequence star with comparatively steady output. Its long lifespan and moderate luminosity allowed Velis to develop an exceptionally old and interconnected biosphere.

nodes.name: Velis I

areas.name: Glassjaw Leases
areas.description: Shielded automated mines extract dense metals from the dayside crust. Human and Korasha maintenance teams enter during short scheduled shutdowns.
areas.gmNotes: Erbium reports the leases as essential to Velish medical infrastructure, allowing any labor disruption to be described as a threat to Second Emergence care.

nodes.description: A small, tidally locked metal-rich world with a molten dayside and airless night hemisphere. Nearly all activity is automated.

nodes.name: Velis II

areas.name: Mirror Vault Platforms
areas.description: High-altitude robotic platforms harvest carbon and sulfur compounds while testing high-temperature metamorphic materials.

nodes.description: A hot greenhouse world beneath dense clouds. It supports remote industrial platforms and short-duration research missions.

nodes.name: Velis

areas.name: Nareth Spires
areas.description: A network of defended canopy cities linked by sealed transit lines. Nareth hosts major Damaya and Korasha schools, diplomatic offices, and Second Emergence clinics.

areas.name: Kethra Continuity Territory
areas.description: A Katalash-majority ecological territory whose settlements, tools, and public spaces were designed around ancestral Lashunta morphology rather than human-standard infrastructure.
areas.gmNotes: The territorial government is divided between preservationists and restorationists. Settled Systems security reports routinely blur the distinction.

areas.name: The Still Choir
areas.description: A vast wetland and seasonal forest where magnetite-bearing fungi, electrically active root networks, and migrating fauna produce powerful natural psionic interference.
areas.gmNotes: Erbium's restricted surveys suggest the region can disrupt ordinary surveillance and telepathic monitoring. Public reports describe the same effect as a neurological hazard.

areas.name: Applied Expression Campus Seven
areas.description: An Erbium-sponsored developmental hospital, school, and placement center providing subsidized Second Emergence treatment through long-term service agreements.
areas.gmNotes: The campus maintains extensive behavioral, genetic, telepathic, and family-network records. Damaya and Korasha programs receive far more funding than Katalash development.

nodes.description: The Lashunta homeworld is a warm, biologically dense planet of towering vegetation, deep wetlands, seasonal forests, and heavily interconnected ecosystems. Natural psionic phenomena arise from the interaction of biological electrical fields, mineral deposits, atmospheric conditions, and mechanisms that remain poorly understood. A young planetary ring complicates orbital traffic and casts moving shadow bands across the biosphere.
nodes.gmNotes: Velis is formally self-governing. Settled Systems authorities and Erbium shape policy through transit certification, medical sponsorship, security cooperation, and ownership of the navigation systems needed to cross the ring safely.

nodes.name: The Crown of Velis
nodes.description: A narrow ring of dark silicate fragments, reflective ice, and charged dust formed from a shattered inner moon. Its shifting shadow bands affect migration and plant behavior across Velis.
nodes.gmNotes: The ring is geologically young. Independent Velish astronomers dispute Erbium's claim that its breakup was entirely natural.

nodes.name: Soryn

areas.name: First Contact Vault
areas.description: A buried Velish archive preserving pre-contact models, Star Dream interpretations, and early records of the Damaya and Korasha development programs.
areas.gmNotes: Several sealed collections contradict Erbium's preferred history of Lashunta convergence.

nodes.description: Velis's surviving major moon. Its regular cycle stabilizes the planet's axial tilt and shapes many seasonal ecological and ceremonial calendars.

nodes.name: Crown Gate Transit Authority
nodes.description: A rotating orbital station coordinating traffic through the Crown of Velis, including debris forecasting, quarantine, customs, and emergency rescue.
nodes.gmNotes: The station is publicly administered, but its navigation models, biometric systems, and security software are licensed from Erbium. Travel permits provide a convenient basis for monitoring Katalash communities and independent medical traffic.
nodes.cargoDescription: Medical supplies, metamorphic chamber components, survey equipment, and ring-clearance drones

nodes.name: Velis IV

areas.name: Beneath Line Survey
areas.description: A mixed Katalash and independent research settlement studying deep ice, mineral formations, and weak psionic effects beneath the crust.

nodes.description: A cold super-Earth with thin air, extensive subsurface ice, and a sparse network of research and extraction settlements.

nodes.name: Velis Main Belt
nodes.description: A broad belt of rocky, metallic, and carbonaceous bodies. Charged dust and dense prospecting traffic made early approaches to Velis difficult before reliable Drift navigation.
nodes.gmNotes: Erbium uses the belt's real navigation hazards to justify exclusive routing, transponder, and inspection requirements throughout the inner system.

nodes.name: Velis V
nodes.description: A large gas giant supporting fuel harvesting, deep-system survey traffic, and a chain of remote research facilities.

nodes.name: Tarev

areas.name: Quiet Depths Laboratory
areas.description: A buried Erbium laboratory studying Lashunta neural development in an environment isolated from Velis's natural psionic background.
areas.gmNotes: The laboratory's developmental experiments are absent from public Second Emergence records.

nodes.description: An ice-covered moon with a deep subsurface ocean. It supplies water and propellant while hosting restricted biological and psionic research.

nodes.name: Velis VI

areas.name: Last Voice Relay
areas.description: The outermost reliable navigation and communications relay in the system, positioned above the ice giant's magnetic poles.

nodes.description: A distant ice giant marking the practical edge of routine Velis-system traffic.

system.notes: Standalone system for Velis, the Lashunta homeworld and origin of the Damaya, Korasha, and Katalash expressions.
system.gmNotes: Velis retains formal political autonomy, but its governments depend on Erbium-owned navigation, medical, developmental, and security infrastructure. The Crown's genuine transit hazards allow surveillance and movement controls to be presented as neutral public safety policy.

system.name: Zakaron System

nodes.name: Zakaron Primary
nodes.description: A mature yellow-orange G-type main-sequence star with steady output. Its long stable period allowed life to develop on Zakaron before the Rupture Wars and now supplies the exterior radiator fields, orbital foundries, and solar-collection infrastructure of the rebuilt system.

nodes.name: Kezhar

areas.name: Dayknife Forges
areas.description: A chain of shielded solar foundries on the permanent dayside that refine refractory metals and manufacture armor ceramics, weapon housings, and radiation-resistant cybernetic components.
areas.gmNotes: Several forge complexes contain sealed pre-Accord production lines whose output never enters public procurement records.

areas.name: The Hollow Cuts
areas.description: A continent-scale field of abandoned shafts and collapsed strip mines left after Zakaron exhausted Kezhar's accessible rare-earth and erbium-bearing formations during the War of the Open Stars.

nodes.description: A tidally locked metal-rich inner world. Its dayside supports automated solar foundries while deep scars across both hemispheres record centuries of extraction that removed nearly every commercially useful erbium-bearing deposit.

nodes.name: Oltara

areas.name: Vapor Works Nine
areas.description: Floating industrial platforms harvest sulfur, carbon, and nitrogen compounds for explosives, propellants, armor polymers, and sealed habitat chemistry.

areas.name: White Flash Range
areas.description: A restricted hemisphere used to test orbital penetrators, plasma weapons, thermal shielding, and autonomous combat systems under crushing pressure and corrosive cloud cover.
areas.gmNotes: The range also tests weapons intended for use against hardened planetary infrastructure similar to Kharosai's gravity and pressure systems.

nodes.description: A hot greenhouse world beneath dense carbon dioxide and sulfurous clouds. Oltara serves as the system's principal atmospheric-chemistry site and a remote weapons-testing environment where failures can be contained far from inhabited Zakaron.

nodes.name: Zakaron

areas.name: Kharosai
areas.description: The continuous inhabited megacity built across the inside of Zakaron's reinforced crust. Artificial gravity pulls residents toward the shell while the opposing districts of the Overcity remain visible across the central cavity.

areas.name: Sairak Axis
areas.description: The fortified capital district containing the Assembly of Holds, Conclave of Veils, Hall of the Paired Mandate, treaty ministries, and the most stable gravity-control region in Kharosai.

areas.name: Kheled Foundry Belt
areas.description: A broad industrial band of shipyards, armor works, implant manufacturers, military laboratories, furnace districts, and freight lines visible across much of the Overcity.
areas.gmNotes: A concealed power draw beneath the district supports an experimental Drift-core program operated by revanchist holds and Madrosarai weapons researchers.

areas.name: The Black Meridian
areas.description: Dense housing, repair markets, illegal clinics, weapons dealers, and clanless communities built across one of the deepest reinforced planetary fractures. Permanent restraints remain standard in homes and workshops because local gravity failures are common.

areas.name: Veilmarket
areas.description: A Madrosarai-dominated commercial and intelligence district known for bloodline clinics, specialized cybernetics, surgical theaters, information brokers, discreet clan compounds, and private security firms.

areas.name: The Ashskin
areas.description: The inhabited boundary between Kharosai and Zakaron's dead exterior. Pressure-sealed settlements support starports, radiator maintenance, orbital defense, salvage crews, and expeditions into pre-Inversion ruins.

areas.name: The Sunlock
areas.description: The technologically stabilized remnant of Zakaron's core, held inside magnetic containment rings and surrounded by thermal exchangers, power-conversion structures, and regulated luminous plasma layers that light Kharosai.
areas.gmNotes: A persistent thermal imbalance in the southern containment ring is real, though covert construction beneath Kheled Foundry Belt is worsening it.

nodes.description: The ancestral world of the Vesk and Madrosarai is externally airless and plated with radiator fields, armored access structures, transit conduits, and orbital defenses. Its population lives across the inner surface of the reinforced crust inside Kharosai, where a maintained atmosphere, overlapping gravity projectors, and the Sunlock preserve a civilization built inside the consequences of the Rupture Wars.
nodes.gmNotes: Zakaron remains the strongest sovereign planetary rival to Erbium Industries. Its government opposes corporate control while preserving authoritarian clan structures, classified weapons programs, and factions that still regard the War of the Open Stars as an interrupted expansion rather than a settled defeat.

nodes.name: Concord High Anchorage
nodes.description: Zakaron's principal civilian orbital port, customs station, diplomatic arrival point, and treaty inspection facility. Most foreign visitors transfer here before entering the armored descent corridors to Kharosai.
nodes.gmNotes: Erbium maintains accredited inspectors and relay technicians aboard the station but possesses no chartered civil authority. Concord security records every corporate movement separately from the PES stamp.
nodes.cargoDescription: Cybernetics, armor components, medical systems, imported food concentrates, relay parts, and sealed erbium consignments

nodes.name: Kheled High Yard
nodes.description: A heavily defended orbital construction complex producing warship hulls, station modules, heavy armor, and commercial vessels. Finished hulls can outnumber the refined Drift cores legally available to power them.
nodes.gmNotes: Several sealed construction cradles contain treaty-limited hulls registered as civil-defense platforms. Their weapon hardpoints and command architecture indicate rapid military conversion.
nodes.cargoDescription: Unfinished hull sections, armor ceramics, reactor components, cybernetic control systems, weapons mounts, and classified military cargo

nodes.name: Marnak

areas.name: Red Archive Range
areas.description: A cold desert weapons range where modern test sites overlap preserved fortifications, wrecked invasion craft, and training grounds from the War of the Open Stars.

areas.name: Seventh Pit
areas.description: The deepest surviving erbium mine in the inner system. It now functions as a geological laboratory and memorial to the extraction surge that supplied Zakaron's first interstellar fleets.
areas.gmNotes: The mine is publicly exhausted. Restricted surveys continue below the declared floor, searching for microdeposits and evidence of deliberately falsified pre-Accord records.

nodes.description: A cold dry world with a thin atmosphere, scattered subsurface ice, extensive military ranges, and exhausted mines. Marnak supplied much of the refined erbium consumed during Zakaron's first expansion and remains a central site of martial memory.

nodes.name: The Spent Crown

areas.name: Still Fleet Necropolis
areas.description: A dispersed field of obsolete warships, stripped Drift hulls, weapons platforms, and captured vessels stored among mined-out asteroids after the Still-Drive Accords.
areas.gmNotes: Some wrecks retain sealed arsenals, dormant autonomous defenses, or navigation records omitted from the accepted war history.

areas.name: The Quiet Foundries
areas.description: A network of low-signature industrial caverns officially registered as reserve civil-defense depots.
areas.gmNotes: Several revanchist holds use the foundries to assemble unregistered fleet components and train crews beyond treaty inspection.

nodes.description: A broad belt of rocky and metallic bodies stripped during Zakaron's interstellar expansion. Abandoned mines, armored habitats, old fleet depots, and military debris make the belt economically depleted and strategically valuable.

nodes.name: Drauk

areas.name: Spearhead Skimmers
areas.description: Armored atmospheric platforms harvest hydrogen isotopes and volatile feedstock for fusion plants, military reserves, and outer-system shipping.

nodes.description: A massive gas giant supporting fuel harvesting, outer-system logistics, and military patrol routes. Its radiation belts and dense moon system conceal ship movements from ordinary civilian tracking.

nodes.name: Kharad

areas.name: Deep Keel Yard
areas.description: A buried military shipyard using Kharad's ice and rock as shielding. It services long-range patrol vessels outside the heavy traffic around Zakaron.

nodes.description: A large ice-rock moon excavated for water, metals, and trace erbium during the expansion era. Modern military yards occupy the strongest surviving caverns beneath its cratered surface.

nodes.name: Nhalet
nodes.description: A distant ice giant marking the outer boundary of routine commercial traffic. Its magnetic poles support communications infrastructure, treaty inspection traffic, and long-duration patrol operations.

nodes.name: Still-Drive Accord Relay
nodes.description: The recognized intersystem communications and navigation relay for Zakaron. The station is jointly administered under the Still-Drive Accords and remains the largest permanent Erbium presence anywhere in the system.
nodes.gmNotes: Erbium controls the authentication hardware and external PES uplink. Concord technicians maintain parallel clocks, traffic records, and navigation archives because either party may dispute the other's stamp during a crisis.
nodes.cargoDescription: Relay components, sealed erbium assemblies, sensor replacements, patrol supplies, and treaty inspection equipment

nodes.name: Varkesh

areas.name: Survey Scar Seven
areas.description: A temporary excavation and sample-processing camp established after remote instruments detected a previously inaccessible erbium-bearing formation beneath the fractured crust.
areas.gmNotes: The public samples understate the concentration. Navigation logs show that the survey ship entered a region excluded from the released mission track.

areas.name: The Buried Lattice
areas.description: A geometrically regular subsurface formation recorded in classified gravimetric scans and described publicly as a mineral fault network.
areas.gmNotes: The formation is an inhabited artificial complex. Its occupants do not satisfy current Concord recognition standards, and the first-contact team classified the structure as an automated extraction installation.

nodes.description: A fractured outer dwarf planet on a steep eccentric orbit. Long considered geologically exhausted, Varkesh recently became the focus of a sealed Concord survey after instruments detected erbium-bearing material beneath its ice and shattered rock.
nodes.gmNotes: Erbium knows that the discovery may invalidate parts of the Still-Drive Accords. The company has delayed intervention because a public treaty crisis would support wider inspection powers and tighter control over independent military fleets.

system.notes: Standalone system for Zakaron, the inverted Vesk and Madrosarai homeworld and the principal military-industrial and cybernetic power independent of direct Erbium administration.
system.gmNotes: Zakaron's system was heavily stripped of erbium during the War of the Open Stars. The Concord remains dependent on controlled imports while maintaining covert fleet programs, parallel time records, and active searches for deposits that could end Erbium's strategic leverage.
